title: Dhammadinna
hook: foremost among nuns in teaching; the Buddha says he would have answered as she did (MN 44)

segments.voice: Yesterday: salla, the arrow of grief Patacara drew out of other mothers' hearts. Your line: from grief to teacher. Today, a nun whose answers the Buddha stood behind.

A man goes to see a nun, and he brings questions. He's Visakha, a lay follower, and he isn't a stranger to her: the commentaries say she had been his wife before she went forth. Her name is Dhammadinna. He sits to one side and starts asking. What is identity? Where does it come from? What path ends it? She answers each one, cleanly. And he keeps going, question after question, until he goes one question too far. This Visakha, by the way, is a man. The laywoman Visakha comes in a few days.
screen: `A MAN WITH QUESTIONS.` → `HIS FORMER WIFE, NOW A NUN.` → `ONE QUESTION TOO FAR.`

segments.voice: First, the questions, in the forty-fourth discourse of the Middle Length collection. They aren't easy. Visakha asks what identity is, and she answers that the teaching calls it the five aggregates people cling to: body, feeling, perception, formations and consciousness. He asks about the noble eightfold path, about meditation, about pleasant and painful feeling and what tendency lies under each one. Her answers are short and exact. Second, the edge. At last he asks: what is the counterpart of nibbana? She stops him. Friend Visakha, you've gone too far; you couldn't find the limit of your questions. The holy life is grounded in nibbana and ends in nibbana. If you wish, go and ask the Buddha, and remember what he tells you. Third, the endorsement. Visakha goes and tells the Buddha the whole conversation. The Buddha says: Dhammadinna is wise, of great wisdom. If you had asked me, I would have answered exactly as she did. That is the meaning; remember it so. Fourth, her title. In the list of foremost disciples, Dhammadinna is named first among the nuns who teach the Dhamma. And notice the echo. Three days ago, Khema answered a king, and the Buddha's answer matched hers. Today the Buddha says it again: the same. The texts make the point twice, on purpose or not: a woman taught, and the teaching stood. She taught him.
screen: `HE ASKS, SHE ANSWERS.` · `"YOU'VE GONE TOO FAR, FRIEND."` · `"I WOULD HAVE ANSWERED THE SAME."` · `FOREMOST AMONG NUNS WHO TEACH.` · then, large: `SHE TAUGHT HIM.`

segments.voice: Think of someone who taught you something that held up, and who also knew where to stop: who said, that's enough for today, or, go and ask someone who knows more. Put what they taught you into one plain sentence, silently, and let thanks come if it comes.
Dhammadinna. The nun named foremost in teaching, whose answers the Buddha said he would have given himself. Today's word.
Your line: she taught him. Her answers needed no correcting. Day seven hundred fifty-nine, done.

howItsDone: The Culavedalla Sutta, Dhammadinna's dialogue with Visakha, is studied in Theravada monasteries and Buddhist study groups as a short, careful teaching on identity, the path and feeling.

fork.reveal: she tells him he has gone too far, that the holy life ends in nibbana, and sends him to the Buddha, who says he would have answered the same.

chat.says: Did the Buddha ever say a woman taught as well as he did?
options: Yes: of Dhammadinna he said, I'd have answered exactly as she did.
No, he corrected her answers before they could be taught to others.
No, the texts only record women listening, never teaching.
chat.meaning: In MN 44, the Buddha calls Dhammadinna wise and says he would have answered Visakha exactly as she did.

Dhammadinna.meaning: a nun named foremost among those who teach the Dhamma

Visakha.meaning: a lay follower who questioned her; her former husband

nibbana.meaning: the end of craving and suffering, the goal of the path

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 1.14 (Dhammadinna foremost among nuns who teach the Dhamma)

notes: All paraphrased; no public-domain translation of MN 44 the writer was certain of.
That Visakha had been Dhammadinna's husband comes from the commentary (Papancasudani), not the sutta; attributed to 'the commentaries'.
Confirm the order and scope of Visakha's questions summarized here (identity, the path, meditation, feeling and the underlying tendencies), and the final 'counterpart' question (nibbana's patibhaga).
Hook flags that this Visakha is not the laywoman Visakha of days 763-764.
Echo with Khema (SN 44.1, day 756) is stated with 'on purpose or not' to avoid claiming design.
